html:
St Martin's Cathedral in Bratislava, then called Pressburg or Pozsony, was the coronation church of the kings of Hungary from 1563 to 1830. Eleven kings and eight queens were crowned in it.

After the defeat at Mohács in 1526 the Ottomans took Buda, and the Habsburgs moved the Hungarian capital and diet to Pressburg in 1536. Among those crowned here was Maria Theresa in 1741. The diet kept meeting in the town until 1848, when the revolution moved government to Pest. Pressburg became Bratislava, capital of Slovakia, only in 1919.
